trailer_schema.policy: Blueprint-first Claude adapter contract. DAG/subagent semantics are defined by inputs/BLUEPRINT.md yaml orchestrator blocks, compiled task packs, hooks, trailers and the state machine. Mutating roles must provide AGENT-scoped trailers, durable handoffs/evidence and legal state transitions. Info-only roles write metadata only. Journey-gate fields are accepted for runtime contract but lifecycle status is still controlled by state-machine.yaml.

closer.transport_completion_policy: For pr-flow, done requires PR_READY=yes, MERGED=yes, CANONICAL_MAIN_SYNCED=yes, plus report/runtime-snapshot/git/push/workflow/runtime/worktree proof and runtime cleanup detail: DOCKER_RUNTIME_CLEANED, RANCHER_RUNTIME_CLEANED and DEV_PORTS_RELEASED must be yes or not_applicable:<reason>. PR open, queued, unmerged, dirty root, cleanup failure or unreleased ports is blocked, not done.

handoff_contract.policy: Every mutating role appends a section to the task handoff and writes/points to durable evidence. Chat-only success is not a valid lifecycle mutation. init-verify-slice may create a non-trailer pending section, but only the final SubagentStop trailer can mutate state.

policy: Main-orchestrator must include Agent and Skill tools when used as --agent; official-docs-researcher must use official documentation sources only.
Active prompts define agent/subagent details: manual memory paths, spawn budget, journey gates, root split, pr-flow, worktree/runtime context and blueprint-first resolved_specs.
notes: keeps inputs/BLUEPRINT.md as the active runtime origin during end-to-end trailer smoke; example blueprints are fixtures, not the packaged active state.

runtime_contract.parallel_locks: DAG emits parallel_groups and task.locks; next-wave selects non-conflicting subsets and claim_task rechecks active blockers under POSIX fcntl locks.
runtime_contract.spawn_budget: Default 70 completed subagents per slice; the 71st Agent spawn is denied by PreToolUse Agent and completed stops are counted by SubagentStop under runtime-state lock.
runtime_contract.journey_gate: Closer can add pending journey verifications from task.closes_journeys; /verify-journey or explicit JOURNEY_VERIFY_OUTCOME clears them. next-wave defers only tasks that reference pending journeys.

next_slice_pipeline.chain: planner -> developer ∥ official-docs-researcher? -> validator ∥ tester -> debugger? -> validator ∥ tester -> slice-maintain -> verify-slice automático
next_slice_pipeline.planner: blocking; prepares task context and NEEDS_OFFICIAL_DOCS before implementation
next_slice_pipeline.developer_parallel_docs: developer and official-docs-researcher run in the same assistant message only when official docs are needed; researcher is info-only
next_slice_pipeline.validator_tester_parallel: validator and tester run in one assistant message after developer; validator is info-only, tester is lifecycle
next_slice_pipeline.debugger_loop: debugger fixes in-scope defects and returns to validator ∥ tester; maximum 4 cycles before blocked
next_slice_pipeline.closure: tester ready_for_close triggers slice-maintain and automatic verify-slice; closer is manual after verified_pending_close

verification_surface.rule: journey_refs alone never require browser/mobile MCP; visual MCP is required only when compiled UI specs, routes, screens or explicit visual/mobile verify modes declare a UI surface.

purpose: Static, machine-readable contract for Claude Code agents, hooks, skills and DAG runtime. Generated state stays outside .claude.

static_config.policy: Agents must not edit static orchestrator config during product-building runs.

dag_scope.policy: DAG-only. Worker identity comes from CLAUDE_ACTIVE_TASK_ID plus CLAUDE_TASK_PACK. No implicit task selector exists.

derived_core_state.policy: Only compiler/bootstrap/claim/hooks/runtime checker scripts may write these files directly under locks.
derived_core_state.canonical_dag_source: registry.json tasks plus task-dag.json topology; check-task-dag --strict rejects drift.

may_write: handoff notes only through scoped workflow
planning notes in active handoff when invoked by next-slice
must_not_write: generated task-packs directly unless explicit maintenance task

may_write: blueprint review notes when explicitly requested
shared config files explicitly declared in the DAG task write_set

must_not_write: product code except explicit fixture/test-only scope

may_write: smallest product-code fix inside TASK_ID write_set

slice-verifier.notes: Human-real verify gate. Writes handoff/evidence only; SubagentStop moves lifecycle when trailer and evidence are valid.

may_write: deployment manifests/config/scripts inside task write_set when deployment is explicitly in scope
must_not_write: deploy to a real target without approved QA/closer gate, dry-run evidence and rollback plan

may_write: lifecycle event artifacts produced by close scripts
must_not_write: Co-authored-by trailers or Claude coauthor metadata in commits
git stash as normal close flow

verify_policy.auto_verify_requires: low risk, deterministic commands, no closing journey, real/provided data evidence
verify_policy.state_machine: tester pass -> ready_for_close; slice-verifier verified -> verified_pending_close; closer committed -> done; issues_found -> needs_debug; blocked stays blocked until rerun by the responsible lifecycle role.
verify_policy.browser_mcp_isolation_policy: Use isolated browser/profile per TASK_ID. Browser/mobile visual verification is required only when verification_surface.requires_visual_mcp=true.
verify_policy.backend_no_ui_policy: For requires_visual_mcp=false, verify real-but-headless evidence using API/DB/worker/dependency/core/log proof; do not block merely because no browser exists.

followup_tasks.purpose: Only work that cannot reasonably be fixed inside the active TASK_ID becomes a formal DAG follow-up. In-scope defects, small fixes inside the current write_set and mechanical runtime retries stay in the same slice via developer/debugger/retest.
followup_tasks.proposal_command: ./scripts/register-followup-task.sh propose --origin-task <TASK_ID> --scope-classification <classification> --repair-decision followup_required|human_decision_required --why-not-debugger <reason> --title <title> --severity blocker|critical|high|medium|low [--files-estimate <n|unknown>] [--fits-current-write-set yes|no|unknown] [--outside-current-write-set yes|no|unknown] [--requires-blueprint-change yes|no|unknown] [--requires-new-dependency yes|no|unknown] [--requires-human-decision yes|no|unknown] [--missing-real-data yes|no|unknown] [--description <text>] [--write-set <path>] [--verify <command/evidence>]
followup_tasks.promotion_policy: Promotion creates a blueprint patch request. It does not mutate registry.json, task-dag.json or runtime-state.json directly. The accepted change must be added to inputs/BLUEPRINT.md and then compile/bootstrap regenerates the DAG.
followup_tasks.policy: Formal follow-ups do not replace debugger/retest for defects inside the active task pack. Workers only report candidates; main-orchestrator/operator promotes or waives. High/critical/blocker proposed follow-ups block new claims until triaged.
followup_tasks.closer_policy: Formal proposed follow-ups from the same origin_task_id may be referenced in the closer report and PR, but closer must not convert them into DAG tasks automatically.
followup_tasks.triage_policy: A follow-up proposal must include explicit repair triage. If the finding fits the current write_set, touches only a few files and needs no blueprint change, new dependency, missing real data or human decision, it must be fixed in the active slice instead of creating a FU.

journey_gate.policy: Pending journeys defer only tasks whose journey_refs or dependencies reference that JID.

verification.shared_file_browser_gate: Tasks touching shared UI/router/provider/layout surfaces must use human browser/mobile verification when verification_surface declares a visual surface.

notes: schema_version fields identify machine-contract schemas, not historical package releases.
Python and GitHub Action version pins are executable runtime alignment constraints.
Dependency version/path checks are generic anti-imposter verification steps.
